title: Numbers
objective: Recognize JavaScript's single number type and convert strings to numbers safely.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Unlike some languages that separate whole numbers from decimals, JavaScript has just one numeric type: Number. 5 and 5.0 and 3.14 are all the same kind of value under the hood, whole numbers included.

Doing math on two numbers gives you a number back, as you'd expect. But text typed by a user, or read from a file, arrives as a string — even if it looks like digits — and JavaScript won't silently treat '5' as the number 5 everywhere.

Number(text) converts a string into a number, raising nothing but returning NaN (Not a Number) if the text can't be parsed. parseInt(text) does something similar but stops at the first non-digit character instead of failing outright, which is handy for text like '20px'.
explanation.rule: Use Number(text) to convert a string into a number before doing math with it.

examples.title: Converting Text to a Number
examples.note: Number('7') becomes the number 7, so adding 3 gives 10 instead of concatenating into '73'.

checks.question: What does "7" + 3 evaluate to in JavaScript?

feedback.correct: Correct — + between a string and a number converts the number to text and concatenates, giving '73'.
feedback.incorrect: Without converting first, + treats a string operand as text — "7" + 3 concatenates into the string '73', not the number 10.

assignment.title: Ingot Count
assignment.brief: Write ingotReport(countText) that converts countText (a string, like '7') to a number, adds 1, and logs the result.
requirements: Convert countText to a number using Number().

hints: Number(countText) converts the string '7' into the actual number 7.
Without converting first, count + 1 on a string would concatenate instead of adding.
Store the converted value in a variable before adding 1 to it.
ingotReport('7') should log exactly 8, not '71' or '7' followed by 1.
